text:
julia: Hey team — customer on prod seeing SSE stream disconnects on Safari intermittently. They report partial final tokens then the client reconnects repeatedly and gets nothing. Chrome / Firefox OK.

julia: App uses EventSource to https://api.redwood.example/streams/chat?session=abc123 and auth via Authorization: Bearer <token>. We recently fronted with a CDN (Cloudflare). Started after that.

julia: Repro steps:
1) open Safari iOS 16.4
2) load page
3) start conversation, observe stream stalls at ~10-20s and then reconnects

julia: Response headers show:
```
content-type: text/event-stream
cache-control: public, max-age=3600
cf-cache-status: HIT
```
julia: Looks like CDN caches the stream. Also saw some 304s in edge logs when client reconnects.

maya (support): Thanks Julia — can you paste the full request headers from the browser and a sample request-id from the response? Also do you see any 401s on reconnects or only empty events?

julia: No 401s, just eventstream closes then reconnects. Request-id on last attempt: rid_03a9. Browser UA: Mozilla/5.0 (iPhone; CPU iPhone OS 16_4 like Mac OS X)...

maya (support): Ok setting P1 and escalating to runtime/infra. Quick hypotheses: CDN is caching streaming endpoint (shouldn't), and Vary or Authorization isn't being respected. Also Safari EventSource may treat 304s / chunked encodings oddly which can drop the open connection.

ash (eng-runtime): Oof. If CDN returns HIT or 304 for SSE that will break the continuous stream — browsers expect a persistent chunked response. Fixes: ensure streaming endpoints have `Cache-Control: no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate` and `Vary: Authorization` or better bypass caching at edge (cache key should not include streams). Also avoid exposing tokens in query string — but Authorization header sometimes gets stripped by CDNs or proxies; verify CF worker isn't removing headers.

miguel (infra): On Cloudflare you need to turn off caching for the path or set `Cache-Control: private, max-age=0, s-maxage=0` and enable `Origin Cache Control: Respect`. Cloudflare will not include Authorization in cache key by default. For some setups `Edge Cache TTL: 0` and Page Rule to bypass is simplest.

ash (eng-runtime): Additional headers that help: `X-Accel-Buffering: no` (nginx) to avoid buffering, `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`, and explicit `Content-Type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8`. Safari is known to collapse idle connections; keepalive comments: send a comment line `: keepalive

` every ~15s to keep connection alive. Also ensure you don't send 304s on reconnection — return full 200 with stream consumed from start or use a separate resume protocol.

maya (support): Can we get a curl repro we can run from support box to see behavior through CDN? Julia, if you can run:
```
curl -v -N -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  "https://api.redwood.example/streams/chat?session=abc123" | hexdump -C
```
This will show if the connection stays open and whether bytes arrive.

julia: Running now — output shows an initial 200 then bytes for ~12s then no more, connection closed by server. Edge logs show `cf-request-id: abc` and `cf-cache-status: HIT` at the same time.

ash (eng-runtime): Confirmed: if the edge serves a cached object or 304, Safari will treat that as a finished response and EventSource won't get further chunks. Short-term workaround: set CDN to bypass for `/streams/*` and add `Cache-Control: no-store` on Redwood responses. Medium-term: route streams to a pass-through subdomain that doesn't sit behind cache.

miguel (infra): I've created a Cloudflare rule to bypass caching for `/streams/*` for the customer's zone. Will also add a transform to preserve Authorization header. Rolling in 10m.

support-bot: Ticket #SUP-9123 created and assigned to eng-runtime (ash). Priority: P1. Logs attached.

julia: Thanks — we'll test after the rule propagates.

maya (support): Follow-up: if customers can't change CDN rules, recommend switching to short-lived session cookie (httpOnly) or websocket which most CDNs treat differently (or use dedicated endpoint behind a non-caching LB). We'll keep you posted.

julia: Confirmed — after bypass rule, Safari stream stays open and full events arrive. Problem solved for now. Thanks everyone :rocket:
